correctness.rationale: For each nonempty set of r cyclic vertices, r! permutations and r*n^(n-r-1) directed rooted forests give the exact kernel (including r=n). Every Hamming-weight-k Walsh coefficient is the Krawtchouk sum over these counts. At n=p^a, the identity v_p(n-d)=v_p(d) for 1<=d<n compares each nonterminal term to (n-1)!, showing all r<=n-2 terms vanish modulo p^(b+a), and r<=n-3 terms modulo p^(b+2a). The n-1 term has valuation b+v_p(k) for 0<k<n; at k=n, cancellation of the n-1 and n terms leaves (n-1)!n(n-2), with all other terms divisible by p^(b+2a), yielding b+a. The trivial eigenvalue n^n has valuation an. Walsh diagonalization is valid over Z_(p) because 2 is a p-adic unit; this proves exact local Smith exponents and rational invertibility. A standalone independent finite checker passed 7,435 exact assertions, including direct self-map enumeration through n=6, all shells at odd prime-power n<=169, and full mod-p matrix ranks for n=3,5,7.

value.rationale: The p-primary Smith spectrum of a natural full-size 2^n-by-2^n integer convolution is a precise invariant of modular information loss; prime-power vertex counts are a natural arithmetic family where its stratification is nontrivial (interior shells split according to v_p(k), with two exceptional modes). It determines every local invariant factor, exact rank after normalization modulo p, the full p-power precision filtration and rational recoverability for an infinite parameter family. These are not merely numeric tests, a renaming of the underlying counting law, or a tiny improvement in a precomputed table. The unresolved other-prime and non-prime-power cases are explicitly limited.
